falsifiable_hypothesis: The strong full orientation-contrast correction overshot because many targetwise contrasts are noisy. Across the three whole-patient inner folds, an empirical-Bayes signal/noise decomposition can shrink uncertain target contrasts toward zero while preserving reproducible orientation nuisance.
component_rule: Orientation A is the leave-one-whole-patient bagged geometry prediction. Orientation B starts from the interpolated-jackknife geometry prediction. No A/B prediction averaging is performed.
calibration_rule: Within each outer-training partition, use only that partition's authenticated three-fold whole-patient OOF bandwidth-0.7 predictions at its already-selected spectral option. For each inner fold k and target t compute c[k,t]=patient_balanced_mean(y-q_A)-patient_balanced_mean(y-q_B). Let cbar[t]=mean_k c[k,t] and v[t]=sample_variance_k(c[k,t])/3. Estimate tau2=max(sample_variance_t(cbar[t])-mean_t(v[t]),0). If tau2=0 set alpha[t]=0; otherwise alpha[t]=tau2/(tau2+v[t]). Apply q_B=q_B,interpolated_jackknife-0.5*alpha[t]*cbar[t]. The 0.5 factor is the exact two-orientation contrast split, not a tuned strength. Orientation A remains unchanged. No outer-held outcomes, fold/target outcome splicing, scalar grid, or protected data enter calibration.

task_contract.ab_rule: average separately costed A/B losses; never average A/B predictions
